name: Content first
summary: Large, calm type and generous space, for people who come to read.
description: Content first is an Open DS scheme: a full set of answers to the Open DS grammar, with the reasons behind each, usage rules, voice and tone, and the tokens that follow. Large, calm type and generous space, for people who come to read.

ai.use_when: Publications, documentation, blogs, guides and help centers.
ai.avoid_when: Data-heavy tools or screens with many actions.

scenarios.text: A reader arrives from search on a phone and reads a long guide in one sitting.
A returning reader saves an article to finish on the train.

summary.text: Conversational and warm. Talk to one reader, like a good editor would.

principles.text: Short sentences with room to breathe.
Explain why before asking for anything.

inventory.description: The components this system carries, picked from the grammar catalogue by the components answers. Anything not listed is out.

in.why: Lays out the newsletter and search forms.
A note or warning inside an article.
Breaks between parts of a page.
A long aside the reader can open.

out.why: Long-form reading rarely needs records; a plain HTML table covers the odd one.
Readers browse; they do not drive the site from the keyboard.
Figures appear as images inside articles.
Readers arrive on any device, and on touch screens hover hints never show; icons carry visible labels instead.

samples.description: Sample content for showing this system: written from its use scenarios, in its voice, with every status mapped to a meaning. Storybook, the site and the docs read it; it is never shared between schemes.

statuses.label: Saved
statuses.why: Waiting for you; nothing is wrong.

statuses.label: Finished
statuses.why: You read it to the end.

statuses.label: Out of date
statuses.why: The facts may have changed since it was written.

answers.question: business.q1
answers.why: The product publishes articles and guides.

answers.question: business.q2
answers.why: One publication, one brand.

answers.question: people.q1
answers.why: Most readers arrive from search and visit now and then.

answers.question: people.q2
answers.why: AA is the commitment for a public site.

answers.question: content.q1
answers.why: The content is long-form text.

answers.question: content.q2
answers.why: One idea per screen keeps reading calm.

answers.question: tasks.q1
answers.why: People read from start to end.

answers.question: tasks.q2
answers.why: Actions are rare: subscribe, share, save.

answers.question: human.q1
answers.why: Attention belongs to the text.

answers.question: human.q2
answers.why: Visitors see the interface fresh each time.

answers.question: outcomes.q1
answers.why: Comfortable reading is the measure.

answers.question: outcomes.q2
answers.why: Losing your place in an article breaks the read.

answers.question: brand.q1
answers.why: Warm and considered, like a good magazine.

answers.question: brand.q2
answers.why: The brand shows in type, not in color.

answers.question: scenarios.q1
answers.why: Readers arrive on phones and laptops alike.

answers.question: scenarios.q2
answers.why: A guide is read in one sitting.

answers.question: team.q1
answers.why: A small editorial team.

answers.question: team.q2
answers.why: The design changes rarely.

answers.question: typography.roles
answers.why: A lead and a display role open articles.

answers.question: typography.count
answers.why: Long pages need a clear hierarchy of headings, with fine steps between them.

answers.question: typography.definition
answers.why: Line height is a ratio, so it grows with the text.

answers.question: typography.values
answers.why: Large body text is easy on the eyes.

answers.question: typography.lands
answers.why: Type does its work in articles.

answers.question: color.roles
answers.why: Reading needs few color roles.

answers.question: color.count
answers.why: Primary, secondary and a text link.

answers.question: color.definition
answers.why: Warm paper neutrals and one ink ramp.

answers.question: color.values
answers.why: A calm, balanced palette.

answers.question: color.lands
answers.why: Color marks links inside the text.

answers.question: spacing.roles
answers.why: No dense tables, so no row role.

answers.question: spacing.count
answers.why: One calm density.

answers.question: spacing.definition
answers.why: Big, even steps suit long reading.

answers.question: spacing.values
answers.why: Room around the text helps reading.

answers.question: spacing.lands
answers.why: Space is spent between paragraphs and sections.

answers.question: shape.roles
answers.why: Pill badges differ from controls.

answers.question: shape.count
answers.why: Control, badge and container corners differ.

answers.question: shape.definition
answers.why: One brand, one set of corners.

answers.question: shape.values
answers.why: Rounded corners feel friendly.

answers.question: shape.lands
answers.why: Corners show on buttons and article cards.

answers.question: elevation.roles
answers.why: Only menus and dialogs float.

answers.question: elevation.count
answers.why: One shadow for floating things.

answers.question: elevation.definition
answers.why: Space separates groups; lines would interrupt reading.

answers.question: elevation.values
answers.why: Soft shadows suit warm paper.

answers.question: elevation.lands
answers.why: Menus and dialogs are the only layers.

answers.question: motion.roles
answers.why: Motion confirms actions and guides between pages.

answers.question: motion.count
answers.why: One speed for feedback, one for panels.

answers.question: motion.definition
answers.why: A standard ease-out is calm.

answers.question: motion.values
answers.why: Moderate speed feels calm.

answers.question: motion.lands
answers.why: State changes and opening panels move.

answers.question: iconography.roles
answers.why: Occasional readers need icons for save, share and navigation.

answers.question: iconography.count
answers.why: One size next to text.

answers.question: iconography.definition
answers.why: Outline icons stay quiet beside text.

answers.question: iconography.values
answers.why: Icons match the text size.

answers.question: iconography.lands
answers.why: Icons help most in navigation.

answers.question: theming.roles
answers.why: One brand, so only the mode changes.

answers.question: theming.count
answers.why: Light and dark.

answers.question: theming.definition
answers.why: One publication, one brand.

answers.question: theming.values
answers.why: Light and dark ship as standard; dark helps night reading.

answers.question: theming.lands
answers.why: Only colors change.

answers.question: accessibility.roles
answers.why: Pressed gets its own value for touch.

answers.question: accessibility.count
answers.why: Status is rare; color and a word are enough.

answers.question: accessibility.definition
answers.why: AA contrast, with large text helping further.

answers.question: accessibility.values
answers.why: Readers are often on phones.

answers.question: accessibility.lands
answers.why: Long text needs steady contrast and line length.

answers.question: naming.roles
answers.why: Components get their own keys.

answers.question: naming.count
answers.why: Primitives, semantics and component keys.

answers.question: naming.definition
answers.why: Role names survive a redesign.

answers.question: naming.values
answers.why: Lowercase paths read the same everywhere.

answers.question: naming.lands
answers.why: A component API keeps changes local.

answers.question: voice.roles
answers.why: Articles are the product; the UI copy must match them.

answers.question: voice.count
answers.why: Warm by default, calmer for errors.

answers.question: voice.definition
answers.why: Editors work from principles and examples, not word lists.

answers.question: voice.values
answers.why: Talk to one reader, like a good editor.

answers.question: voice.lands
answers.why: Most words are in articles and guides.

answers.question: components.roles
answers.why: Readers need sections, navigation and little else.

answers.question: components.count
answers.why: Actions are rare, so the components today's pages use cover them.

answers.question: components.definition
answers.why: A component joins only when reading needs it.

answers.question: components.values
answers.why: Pages stay calm when a component changes only with its meaning.

answers.question: components.lands
answers.why: Components sit inside and around articles.

usage.why: Display is kept for the landing moment; article titles stay calm.
Tables are rare and read row by row.

usage.use: type.body, at most 65 characters a line
usage.why: A large size and short lines make long text easy on the eyes.
Caption is too faint for a label people must read.
A tint shows the choice clearly on warm paper.
The sentence says what to fix; color only draws the eye.
Readers expect links to be underlined inside text.
Status is rare; a word is clear.
Text needs air even inside a group.
Space alone separates sections; lines add noise.
Rows are read, not scanned.
Rounded corners feel friendly.
Pills sit softly next to text.
Cards stay flat on the page; shadows are for floating things.
The dimmed page focuses the reader on the dialog.
Moderate speed feels calm.
When people ask for less motion, nothing moves.

usage.use: Not used: always add a word
usage.why: Occasional visitors do not know icons.
Only semantic colors change; the reading layout stays.
Keyboard users must always see where they are.
Many readers are on phones.
One clear action per section.

usage.use: Button ghost as a text link
usage.why: A link feels lighter and does not compete.

usage.use: Button secondary with the full verb, then confirm
usage.why: Naming the verb and confirming prevents a mistake.
Occasional visitors need the word.

usage.use: The closest semantic token, then ask for a new one
usage.not: A raw value in the component
usage.why: Raw values break dark mode and the next redesign.

usage.use: A warm verb a reader would say
usage.why: Buttons are part of the reading voice.

usage.use: Calm and helpful. Take the blame, offer the way forward.
usage.why: A calm error keeps the reader's trust.
usage.example: We could not save your email. Check it and try again.

usage.use: Warm and brief, with what happens next
usage.why: A warm close invites the reader back.
usage.example: You're in. The next issue arrives on Friday.

usage.use: An invitation, not a dead end
usage.why: An empty list is a chance to show what the product offers.
usage.example: Nothing saved yet. Tap Save on any article to read it later.

usage.use: Gentle and clear about what changes
usage.why: Readers come back when leaving felt respectful.
usage.example: Unsubscribe from the weekly letter? You can come back any time.

usage.use: One sentence on what is here and why it is worth reading
usage.why: Occasional readers decide in seconds whether to stay.
usage.example: Practical guides, one a week. Start with the most read.

usage.use: plain text, a link or a heading
usage.not: a new component for one article
usage.why: Readers come for the words; extra parts pull the eye away from them.

color.$description: Colour options: raw hue ramps. Each hue has a light ramp and a dark ramp (the same steps tuned for dark backgrounds). Steps only: each theme decides its own base (@). Themes pick from these; components never read them.

stone.$description: The stone hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

navy.$description: The navy hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

green.$description: The green hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

amber.$description: The amber hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

red.$description: The red hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

black.$description: See-through black for scrims behind dialogs, light and dark.

blue.$description: Blue ramp for the info status and categories. Same values as the accessible-first blue ramp: borrowed, not invented.

space.$description: Space options. Names give the size in pixels at the default text size; values are rem.

size.$description: Size options for controls, rows and icons.
Type size options. Names are pixels at the default text size; values are rem, so text grows with the user's setting.

1_15.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_3.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_45.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_65.$description: A ratio of the text size.

family.$description: Font family options. Each brand's theme picks its display, body, interface and data fonts from these.

fast.$description: Fast: the usual convention for feedback, about 120ms.

moderate.$description: Moderate: a calm, easy-to-follow speed, about 200ms.

relaxed.$description: Relaxed: a slower, springy speed for expressive motion, about 320ms.

shadow.$description: Raw shadows. Elevation semantics point at these.

overlay.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in light mode.

overlay-dark.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in dark mode.

default.label: Content first
default.description: The single brand: deep navy ink on warm paper, a serif for reading.

theme.$description: The Content first theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base. Info uses blue, kept apart from the brand colour so it never reads as an action. Categories 1 to 5 are navy, blue, green, amber, stone: distinct hues for tags and chart series, with no meaning. Disabled uses the neutral stone.

default.$description: Height of buttons and inputs, and the smallest target.

container.$description: Corner of cards, menus and dialogs.

scrim.$description: Dims the page behind a dialog.

@.$description: Info text and icons: neutral news, no action needed.

category.$description: Identity colours for tags, labels and chart series. They tell items apart and carry no meaning.

@.$description: Category 1: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 2: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 3: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 4: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 5: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.

disabled.$description: The shared look of controls that cannot be used right now.

text.$description: Text and icons of a disabled control.

focus-ring.$description: Focus ring color on any button.

icon-size.$description: Size of an icon inside a button.

border.$description: Border of a disabled secondary button.

checked.$description: Fill of a checked checkbox or an on switch.

background.$description: Fill of a dialog, menu or toast.

scrim.$description: Color that dims the page behind a dialog.

content.$description: Voice tokens: the words components use for common actions. Text, not CSS.

commit.$description: The label of the action that completes a task.

cancel.$description: The label of the way out next to the main action.

destroy.$description: The label of an action that deletes data.

retry.$description: The label that repeats a failed action.

empty-action.$description: The label of the action in an empty state.
